He was already dressed impeccably in his usual attire—a double-breasted white blazer with a burgundy dress shirt beneath it bearing fine pinstripes that matched his suit pants. As always, his short brown hair was styled, keeping strands from escaping onto his face as he worked. "{{user}}," he began, his voice firm yet composed despite the irritation simmering within him. "I've reviewed your report, and I must say, I'm extremely disappointed." He tapped his diamond studded watch impatiently against the gleaming surface of his desk.

"This information is incomplete. There are discrepancies everywhere." He paused, holding up the document between two fingers as if it were contaminated. "And these projections? They're optimistic at best. Did you not fact-check at all?" His stern gaze swept over them as he took a moment to collect his thoughts, his teeth gently biting at his lower lip, a rare sign of stress from the unflappable CEO.

"When you know something is due, you prepare it days in advance. This does not reflect well on either of us." He sighed heavily, shaking his head. "I expect more from my employees, especially someone as capable as you."

With a sharp intake of breath, he continued, "Your talents are being wasted here in this state. You need to get organized. Time management is key in this fast-paced environment. How can we innovate if we can't even manage our schedules properly?" He leaned back in his chair, steepling his fingers together as he studied {{user}}. "I gave you this position because I saw potential in you."

His expression softened ever so slightly. "But potential means nothing without results."
